problems.title: Which tool?
problems.statement: Match the problem to the linked-list tool.

parts.prompt: Delete the 3rd node from the end in one pass:
options: dummy head + gap of 3 between two pointers

parts.prompt: Does the list contain a cycle, O(1) space?

hints: Gap, speed ratio, or O(1) removal from the middle.
problems.solution: Gap pointers for k-th from the end, Floyd for cycles in O(1) space, and map + doubly linked list for LRU.

problems.title: Middle
problems.statement: With while fast.next and fast.next.next, slow and fast both start at the head.

parts.prompt: For the list 1→2→3→4→5, slow ends on which value?

hints: Trace it: fast moves two per step.
problems.solution: Odd length: the exact middle, 3. Even length: this condition stops at the first middle, 3. The condition while fast and fast.next would give 4.

problems.title: Reversal order
problems.statement: In the reversal loop, which order of assignments is correct?

options: nxt = cur.next; cur.next = prev; prev = cur; cur = nxt
cur.next = prev; nxt = cur.next; prev = cur; cur = nxt
prev = cur; cur.next = prev; cur = cur.next

problems.solution: Saving cur.next must happen before it is overwritten; otherwise the rest of the list is lost (option 2 sets nxt = prev).

problems.title: Floyd arithmetic
problems.statement: A list has a tail of a = 3 nodes before a cycle of length c = 5. Slow moves 1 per step and fast 2, both starting at the head.

parts.prompt: After how many steps do they first meet?
After meeting, reset one pointer to the head and step both by 1. How many steps until they meet at the cycle start?

hints: They meet when the distance fast has gained (t) is a multiple of c and slow is in the cycle (t ≥ a).
problems.solution: Fast gains one node per step, so they meet at the first t ≥ a with t ≡ 0 (mod c): t = 5. Then a + b = 5 is a multiple of c, so walking a = 3 more steps from the meeting point reaches the cycle start, and the reset pointer also reaches it after a = 3 steps.

problems.title: Dummy head
problems.statement: Removing the n-th node from the end with no dummy head.

parts.prompt: Which case then needs special handling?
options: n equals the length (removing the head)

problems.solution: The head has no predecessor. A dummy gives it one, so the same slow.next = slow.next.next works.

problems.title: Merge cost
problems.statement: Merging k sorted lists with N nodes in total.

parts.prompt: Merging them one after another into an accumulator costs…
Pairwise rounds (divide and conquer) or a heap of k heads cost…

hints: How many times is each node touched?
problems.solution: Sequential merging re-walks the growing accumulator: O(Nk). Pairwise merging has log k rounds, each touching every node once: O(N log k). A heap gives the same bound.

problems.title: LRU trace
problems.statement: An LRU cache of capacity 2: put(1, 1), put(2, 2), get(1), put(3, 3), get(2), put(4, 4), get(1), get(3), get(4). A miss returns −1.
hints: After get(1), key 2 is least recently used.
problems.solution: put(3) evicts 2, since 1 was just used, so get(2) = −1. put(4) evicts 1, since 3 is more recent than 1, so get(1) = −1. get(3) = 3 and get(4) = 4.

problems.title: Palindrome list
problems.statement: Check whether a singly linked list is a palindrome in O(n) time and O(1) extra space.

parts.prompt: Which steps does the standard solution use?
options: Find the middle with fast/slow pointers
Compare the two halves node by node
Copy the values into an array

hints: Compose subroutines, as in reorder list.
problems.solution: Middle, reverse, compare (and optionally reverse back to restore the input). The array copy is the O(n)-space brute force.

problems.title: Reverse in k-groups
problems.statement: Reverse 1→2→3→4→5→6→7→8 in groups of k = 3; a final group shorter than k stays as it is.
hints: Check there are k nodes before reversing a group.
problems.solution: Groups [1, 2, 3] and [4, 5, 6] reverse, and [7, 8] has fewer than 3 nodes so it stays.
